arxiv-1907-12836.title: Quantitative rates of convergence to equilibrium for the Degenerate linear Boltzmann equation on the Torus Thanks: ∗ Warwick Mathematics Institute Thanks: ∗∗ LJAD, Université Côte d’Azur
arxiv-1907-12836.creator: Josephine Evans ∗, Iván Moyano ∗∗
arxiv-1907-12836.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Josephine Evans ∗, Iván Moyano ∗∗. We study the linear relaxation Boltzmann equation on the torus with a spatially varying jump rate which can be zero on large sections of the domain. In [ 5 ] Bernard and Salvarani showed that this equation converges exponentially fast to equilibrium if and only if the jump rate satisfies the geometric control condition of Bardos, Lebeau and Rauch [ 3 ] .

arxiv-2006-05356.title: Scalable Thompson Sampling using Sparse Gaussian Process Models
arxiv-2006-05356.creator: Sattar Vakili, Henry Moss, Artem Artemev, Vincent Dutordoir, Victor Picheny
arxiv-2006-05356.description: Abstract Thompson Sampling (TS) from Gaussian Process (GP) models is a powerful tool for the optimization of black-box functions. Although TS enjoys strong theoretical guarantees and convincing empirical performance, it incurs a large computational overhead that scales polynomially with the optimization budget.

arxiv-2010-13893.title: A systematic approach to general higher-order majorization-minimization algorithms for (non)convex optimization
arxiv-2010-13893.creator: Ion Necoara, Daniela Lupu
arxiv-2010-13893.description: Abstract Majorization-minimization algorithms consist of successively minimizing a sequence of upper bounds of the objective function so that along the iterations the objective decreases. Such a simple principle allows to solve a large class of optimization problems, even nonconvex and nonsmooth.

arxiv-2208-11494.title: Vortex Pinning in Neutron Stars, Slip-stick Dynamics, and the Origin of Spin Glitches
arxiv-2208-11494.creator: Bennett Link, Yuri Levin
arxiv-2208-11494.description: Abstract We study pinning and unpinning of superfluid vortices in the inner crust of a neutron star using 3-dimensional dynamical simulations. Strong pinning occurs for certain lattice orientations of an idealized, body-centered cubic lattice, and occurs generally in an amorphous or impure nuclear lattice.

arxiv-2303-12686.title: SRG/eROSITA and XMM-Newton observations of Vela Jr
arxiv-2303-12686.creator: Francesco Camilloni, Werner Becker, Peter Predehl, Konrad Dennerl, Michael Freyberg, Martin G. F. Mayer, Manami Sasaki
arxiv-2303-12686.description: Abstract Context. The Vela supernova remnant complex is a region containing at least three supernova remnants: Vela, Puppis A, and Vela Jr. With the launch of the spectro-imaging X-ray telescope eROSITA on board the Spectrum Roentgen Gamma ( SRG ) mission, it became possible to observe the one degree wide Vela Jr in its entirety.

arxiv-2405-01067.title: AB-Training: A Communication-Efficient Approach for Distributed Low-Rank Learning
arxiv-2405-01067.creator: 1 st Daniel Coquelin, 2 nd Katherina Flügel, 3 rd Marie Weiel, 4 th Nicholas Kiefer, 5 th Muhammed Öz, 6 th Charlotte Debus, 7 th Achim Streit, 8 th Markus Götz
arxiv-2405-01067.description: Abstract Communication bottlenecks severely hinder the scalability of distributed neural network training, particularly in high-performance computing (HPC) environments. We introduce AB-training , a novel data-parallel method that leverages low-rank representations and independent training groups to significantly reduce communication overhead. Our experiments demonstrate an average reduction in network traffic of approximately 70.

dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-1.title: Dio's Roman History, Vol. 1: Books I-XI (Fragments)
dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-1.creator: Dio Cassius (Earnest Cary, trans.)
dio-cassius-roman-history-cary-vol-1.description: Dio Cassius's Roman History (c. 230 CE), fragments of Books 1-11, from the foundation of Rome through the Punic Wars, preserved in Byzantine excerpts, in Earnest Cary's 1914-1927 Loeb translation via Internet Archive (English text only). The 80-book history of Rome from Aeneas to Severus Alexander — the fullest surviving Roman narrative of the Republic's fall and the Empire's first two centuries.

europmc-pmc2756586.title: Metagenomic analysis of respiratory tract DNA viral communities in cystic fibrosis and non-cystic fibrosis individuals.
europmc-pmc2756586.creator: Willner D, Furlan M, Haynes M, Schmieder R, Angly FE, Silva J, Tammadoni S, Nosrat B, Conrad D, Rohwer F.
europmc-pmc2756586.description: The human respiratory tract is constantly exposed to a wide variety of viruses, microbes and inorganic particulates from environmental air, water and food. Physical characteristics of inhaled particles and airway mucosal immunity determine which viruses and microbes will persist

pmc-11322649.title: Orange maker: a CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing and screening project to generate orange-eyed DarkJedi GAL4 lines by undergraduate students
pmc-11322649.creator: Hee Su Park, Anna C Gross, Seungjae Oh, Nam Chul Kim
pmc-11322649.description: One of the greatest strengths of Drosophila genetics is its easily observable and selectable phenotypic markers. The mini-white marker has been widely used as a transgenic marker for Drosophila transgenesis. Flies carrying a mini-white construct can exhibit various eye colors ranging from pale orange to intense red, depending on the insertion site and gene dosage.

pmc-11391504.title: Efficacy and safety of nanoparticle albumin‑bound paclitaxel compared with solvent‑based paclitaxel in adjuvant therapy for breast cancer: A retrospective study
pmc-11391504.creator: Huina Lv, Yanyan Hong, Yuting Zhang, Siyu Li, Bingbing Li, Mingjun Zhang
pmc-11391504.description: The current evidence for the use of nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel (nab-PTX) for adjuvant breast cancer chemotherapy is insufficient. The present study aimed to assess the efficacy and toxicity of nab-PTX in comparison with solvent-based paclitaxel (sb-PTX) in postoperative adjuvant breast cancer treatment.

pmc-11422253.title: Neurological complications in oncology and their monitoring and management in clinical practice: a narrative review
pmc-11422253.creator: Stefanie Fischer, Malte von Bonin, Martin Bornhäuser, Christian Beste, Tjalf Ziemssen
pmc-11422253.description: ImportanceNew anti-tumor treatments, such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and CAR T-cell therapy, are associated with an increasing number of neurological issues linked to tumors not arising from nervous system such as neurological and neuropsychological side effects that can significantly impair quality of life in the short or long term.

pmc-11483836.title: Exploring the management and treatment of IBD from the perspective of psychological comorbidities
pmc-11483836.creator: Lijuan Feng, Xunchao Cai, Qian Zou, Yao Peng, Long Xu, Linlin Wang, Qing Liu, Ting Lou
pmc-11483836.description: The prevalence of anxiety, depression, and other psychological comorbidities among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) significantly exceeds that of the general population. Moreover, a bidirectional relationship exists between psychological comorbidities and IBD. This intricate interplay has substantial clinical implications, impacting treatment adherence, therapeutic efficacy, and disease recurrence rates.

pmc-11546159.title: CAR-T cells based on a TCR mimic nanobody targeting HPV16 E6 exhibit antitumor activity against cervical cancer
pmc-11546159.creator: Zhijian Duan, Dan Li, Nan Li, Shaoli Lin, Hua Ren, Jessica Hong, Christian S. Hinrichs, Mitchell Ho
pmc-11546159.description: The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of human papillomavirus (HPV) are considered promising targets for HPV-related cancers. In this study, we evaluated novel T cell receptor mimic (TCRm) nanobodies targeting the E629-38 peptide complexed with human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A∗02:01 in the chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) format. We isolated two dromedary camel nanobodies, F5 and G9, through phage display screening.

pmc-11669373.title: Development and Usability of an Advance Care Planning Website (My Voice) to Empower Patients With Heart Failure and Their Caregivers: Mixed Methods Study
pmc-11669373.creator: Chetna Malhotra, Alethea Yee, Chandrika Ramakrishnan, Sanam Naraindas Kaurani, Ivy Chua, Joshua R Lakin, David Sim, Iswaree Balakrishnan, Vera Goh Jin Ling, Huang Weiliang, Lee Fong Ling, Kathryn I Pollak
pmc-11669373.description: BackgroundWeb-based advance care planning (ACP) interventions offer a promising solution to improve ACP engagement, but none are specifically designed to meet the needs of patients with heart failure and their caregivers.ObjectiveWe aimed to develop and assess the usability and acceptability of a web-based ACP decision aid called “My Voice,” which is tailored for patients with heart failure and their caregivers.

pmc-12563777.title: Mini-Trampoline Training Enhances Executive Functions and Motor Skills in Preschoolers
pmc-12563777.creator: Mohamed Amine Ltifi, Yosser Cherni, Elena Adelina Panaet, Cristina Ioana Alexe, Helmi Ben Saad, Ana Maria Vulpe, Dan Iulian Alexe, Mohamed-Souhaiel Chelly, Jakub Gąsior
pmc-12563777.description: Highlights What are the main findings? •Mini-trampoline training over 12 weeks improved motor abilities such as functional mobility, postural steadiness, and lower body strength in preschool children.•The intervention also enhanced executive functions, particularly inhibitory control, supporting early cognitive development. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-13031307.title: Linvoseltamab versus real-world International Myeloma Working Group standard-of-care in triple-class exposed relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
pmc-13031307.creator: Shaji Kumar, Sundar Jagannath, Katja C. Weisel, Laura Rosiñol, Xavier Leleu, Meletios-Athanasios Dimopoulos, Efstathios Kastritis, David S. Siegel, Jorge Monge, Juan Du, Javier de la Rubia, Pedro Asensi Cantó, Jae Hoon Lee, María-Victoria Mateos, Borja Puertas, Alessandro Gozzetti, Dominik Dytfeld,
pmc-13031307.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). LINKER-MM1 (NCT03761108) is a Phase 1/2 study of linvoseltamab, a human BCMA×CD3 bispecific antibody for patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) who are triple-class exposed (TCE) with ≥ 3 prior lines of therapy (3L+), or triple-class refractory (TCR). To contextualize efficacy data from LINKER-MM1, the Phase 2 linvoseltamab 200 mg cohort (N = 105) was compared with an international external control arm (ECA) comprising 203 patients from participating International Myeloma Working Group sites who met LINKER-MM1 eligibility criteria based on chart reviews.

pmc-13143451.title: Real-World Hospitalization Outcomes with On-Line Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis
pmc-13143451.creator: Yan Zhang, Anke Winter, Linda H. Ficociello, Belén Alejos Ferrera, Paola Carioni, Christian Apel, Otto Arkossy, Michael Anger, Robert Kossmann, Len A. Usvyat, Stefano Stuard
pmc-13143451.description: Visual Abstract Introduction Patients on chronic hemodialysis bear a high burden of disease and are at a particularly high risk of mortality and hospitalization, with cardiovascular events and infection-related complications representing the greatest drivers for these events.1–5 Inpatient hospitalizations among patients with ESKD in the United States account for nearly half of total Medicare expenses in this patient population.

pmc-13173724.title: Investigation of cellular senescence in the mouse liver caused by low dose fractionated X-ray therapy
pmc-13173724.creator: Xin Lan, Lina Cai, Lingyu Zhang, Yashi Cai, Linqian Zhou, Weiyi Ke, Guanyou Chen, Yanting Chen, Xiaoman Zhou, Weixu Huang, Jianming Zou, Huifeng Chen
pmc-13173724.description: BackgroundThe expanding use of medical diagnostics and radiotherapy has increased public exposure to low dose ionizing radiation (LDIR). A more clinically pressing concern, however, is the unintended irradiation of normal tissues adjacent to the radiotherapy target. Notably, the biological effects of lower cumulative doses on the liver remain poorly characterized.
